items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So when we would play those things where we were both playing at the same time — and that’s dangerous territory — we could do it just like it was written out for us.

ctx.x: Tell us about some of your duo work with Joe Pass.

Well God bless him. I loved him and he was my favorite guitarist and still is. And we had a way of playing. We could play, we knew how to back each other up, but then we could both play at the same time you know? You may have heard us do that. I mean both soloing at the same time. And that, I was going to say, could be difficult. It can be difficult but with him, we knew, we just fit with each other. But the reason, we’re both very selfless you know — he towards my playing and I towards his playing. So when we…

items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: So one time we decided to play together. And we packed the place. So after that when we played, we played together.

ctx.x: It was the name of a club. So one time we decided to play together. And we packed the place. So after that when we played, we played together.
I’m always curious about how two chordal instruments communicate when you’re playing a tune, when you decide to go somewhere else with it.
